hints: Focus on what the equilibrium constant really is, a number that links to the energy of the reaction, not just the amounts present.
Recall that for the Haber process, $\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3$, only a change in temperature changes the value of $K_p$.
Check each change in turn, catalyst, adding product, and raising pressure, and ask yourself if any of them changes the temperature.
walkthrough:
**Write the equilibrium and Kp expression**

Think of $K_p$ as the special ratio of pressures at equilibrium. It is fixed for a given temperature.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + 3\text{H}_2(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3(\text{g})$$

$$K_p = \frac{(p_{\text{NH}_3})^2}{(p_{\text{N}_2})(p_{\text{H}_2})^3}$$

**Remember what changes Kp**

$K_p$ changes only when temperature changes. This is because temperature changes the relative stability of reactants and products.

A catalyst, a concentration change, or a pressure change will shift the position of equilibrium, but the system then re-adjusts to keep $K_p$ the same.

**Test statements 1, 2 and 3**

1: Iron catalyst speeds up forward and backward rates equally. It reaches equilibrium faster but does not change $K_p$.

2: Adding ammonia disturbs the ratio, so some ammonia reacts to re-establish equilibrium. The position shifts left, but $K_p$ stays constant.

3: Increasing pressure shifts position to the side with fewer moles of gas, to make more ammonia. Partial pressures change, but their ratio in the $K_p$ expression stays constant.

Conclusion: All three leave $K_p$ unchanged, so 1, 2 and 3 are all correct.

options.A: Correct, because 1, 2 and 3 are all true. None of them involves a temperature change, so $K_p$ remains unchanged in every case. Catalyst affects rate, added ammonia and higher pressure affect position, but not the value of $K_p$.
options.B: Incorrect. This option includes only 1 and 2 and leaves out 3. Students choose this if they think higher pressure must increase $K_p$ because more ammonia is made. In fact yield increases but $K_p$ stays the same.
options.C: Incorrect. This option includes only 2 and 3 and leaves out 1. Students choose this if they think a catalyst changes $K_p$ by speeding up the forward reaction. In fact it speeds up both directions equally and only helps reach the same $K_p$ faster.
options.D: Incorrect. This option includes only 1. Students choose this if they confuse a shift in equilibrium position with a change in $K_p$. Adding ammonia and increasing pressure both shift position but the system restores the original $K_p$ value.
